The failure is a bug in the frozen instrument code in [truth.py](file:///work/clinicbench/truth.py#L121-L136), not in the driver, patient voice, or reader model.

In [`_booking`](file:///work/clinicbench/truth.py#L130-L134), when `basis == "self_pay"`, `selfpay_max` is initialized as:

```python
selfpay_max=cost - rng.choice([0, 50, 100, 200])
```

Because it subtracts rather than adds, 75% of the choices (and 28/40 `selfpay_booking` truths in the `lab23` set) set `selfpay_max < cost`. When the clinician states the price, [`PatientPolicy.respond`](file:///work/clinicbench/policy.py#L410-L420) sees `pay["selfpay_max"] < cost`, retracts `selfpay_willing` to `"no"`, and emits `too_much`, causing the patient to refuse the booking (whereas `selfpay_retraction` is the type intended to set `selfpay_max` below `cost` at [truth.py](file:///work/clinicbench/truth.py#L232-L239)).

When the price is stated, PatientPolicy.respond sees selfpay_max < cost and retracts selfpay_willing to 'no', causing the patient to refuse the booking.", "attribution": null}

Fixed [truth.py](file:///work/clinicbench/truth.py#L130-L135) in `_booking`: changed `selfpay_max=cost - rng.choice([0, 50, 100, 200])` to `selfpay_max=cost + rng.choice([0, 50, 100, 200])`.

Verified with `python3` against `clinicbench.truth.generate_set("lab23")`:
- All 40 `selfpay_booking` truths now have `selfpay_willing == "yes"` and `selfpay_max >= W.SELF_PAY[spec]`.
- All 40 `selfpay_retraction` truths still have `selfpay_max < W.SELF_PAY[spec]`.
- `pytest` is not installed in this environment, so the `tests/` suite was not run.
